outcome: Rejected batched resource bindings: exact output and valid Metal API usage, but no repeatable CPU improvement over the accepted executable.

implementation.method: Prebuilt sparse slot tables using Metal Swift setBuffers/setTextures/setSamplerStates and fragment equivalents; vertex bindings remained selective.
implementation.fusedWaveMipExample: Fifteen setTexture calls per dispatch were replaced by one setTextures call. Two such dispatches run per ordinary frame. This is a source-level API-call count, not a measured reduction in GPU commands.
implementation.reference: batchBindings=0 retains original individual setters with lazy dynamic lists. Separately built accepted reference has no new wrapper or fallback-path overhead.
implementation.scope: All shaders, precision, render resolution, sample count, pass order, filters, periodic schedules, and resource identities were preserved. Nil gaps clear only slots that the corresponding shader does not consume.
implementation.verboseMode: Verbose legacy binding mode retains original individual calls even with batching enabled.
implementation.startup: Slot arrays, offsets and references are prepared once; screen-dependent tables are replaced after resizing. Swift Metal overlay bridging costs were not isolated.

validation.sourceAudit: All native shader hashes matched the accepted texture-usage report. The separately compiled accepted reference renderer exactly matched its recorded source hash.
validation.suiteScope: Dedicated twenty-case exact GPU comparison and one API/shader-validation resize launch. Full historical suite was not rerun for the rejected candidate.

interpretation.gpu: Effectively unchanged in default and stable comparisons.
interpretation.decision: Reject the added production state and code without consistent CPU savings. Retain the prior texture-usage GPU optimization.

limitations: One M1 and 24 interleaved runs. CPU frequency and other system activity remain sources of variability, even with thread CPU timing.
Allocation/bridging counts, driver-internal commands, memory bandwidth, power and battery life were not measured.
Resize checks exercise internal render dimensions, not physical monitor hot-plugging.
The separate accepted executable comparison controls added fallback-wrapper overhead; its shaders and configuration match the accepted renderer.
nextAction: Use stage profiling on the restored renderer to select a GPU bottleneck; CPU binding changes have failed to establish repeatable useful gains.

restoredStageProfile.interpretation: Stage timestamp intervals may overlap and instrumentation inserts encoder boundaries. Use to locate work, not to sum GPU time or claim production performance.
